upstream.authority: source-lineage inspiration only; not PM canon unless later accepted and compiled

upstream_summary: Coasts describes itself as `Coasts (Containerized Hosts)`: a CLI, daemon, and web UI for multiple isolated development environments built around Git worktrees.

Core concepts include `Coastfile`, build-once/run-many instances, dynamic ports for every instance, checked-out canonical localhost ports for one active instance, offline-first local operation, local HTTPS/root-CA handling, and optional remote service control through SSH tunnels.
Runtime support is centered on `dind`; upstream names `sysbox` and `podman` but says only Docker-in-Docker is wired/tested. DinD uses `docker:dind` with `--privileged`.

Coasts separates build artifacts from running instances; build artifacts contain resolved config, rewritten compose, cached image tarballs, and manifests while secrets are extracted/encrypted separately.

Coasts includes concepts worth considering for PM: Host/Instance/Build/Port/Assignment separation, dynamic/canonical ports, primary-port quick links, private paths, shared service groups, clean test variants, snapshot-seeded volumes, logs/exec/service controls, and integration-test scenarios.
upstream_risks: Do not copy privileged DinD as PM's canonical architecture without explicit capability and security gates.
Do not claim `sysbox` or `podman` support without PM-owned tests.
Do not blindly copy permissive local API/CORS posture, WebSocket terminal controls, file controls, or service mutation controls.

Host command secret extractors, Keychain/file/env extraction, bind mounts, SSH tunnels, remote passwordless sudo, `/data` mounts, rsync/mutagen sync, and `GatewayPorts clientspecified` all need PM-owned permission, FileSafe, redaction, and receipt treatment.

canonical_plan_evidence.summary: Canonical owner for Docker Manager, Docker/Compose/Kubernetes/Unraid surfaces, project-focused Docker Manager subviews, lifecycle/logs/inspect/attach/shell/stats/open-app minima, Compose scenarios for preview/test/development, access intelligence, cleanup advice, host policy, trust/proxy, and event-family registration.

Canonical owner for automated test discovery, capability reports, harness probes, strategy binding, receipts, screenshots/logs/browser/GUI/device evidence, blockers/gaps, and the rule that missing verification records blockers rather than pretending completion.
Canonical GUI direction is Rust + Slint with Docker Manager as a side-panel surface; no React/JS/HTML/CSS GUI transplant for PM.
Docker Manager commands live in `cmd.docker.*`; mutation semantics should route through canonical command ownership, not ad hoc upstream API actions.
Discovery is not execution approval; auto-discovered executable surfaces require permission before load/run.
Filesystem/spawn/runtime transport flows fail closed when guard-visible inputs are missing or stale and must preserve recovery/event logging.
Runtime evidence such as file changes, validation evidence, screenshots, browser recordings, traces, logs, receipts, retention, and redaction belongs in Runtime Artifacts.

subagent_synthesis.summary: PM already has canonical Docker Manager and testing owners; no current canonical Coasts-specific feature exists. Native implementation is aligned if scoped through Docker Manager, ATS, Executor/Run Modes, Permissions/FileSafe, Contracts/storage, and Runtime Artifacts.

No new owner doc is needed by default. Container host definitions route to Containers; testing to Automated Testing; lifecycle dispatch to Executor/Run Modes; storage/events to Contracts/storage; GUI to Docker Manager; permissions/security to Permissions/FileSafe; provider/tool integration to Tools/MCP/CLI providers.

Primary drift risks are accidental runtime unlock, duplicate Docker/control-plane ownership, FileSafe/storage bypass, testing harness confusion, separate website/upstream transplant, host identity drift, and secret leakage.
Suggested MVP: reusable host templates, run/stop/reset instances for project testing, Automated Testing binding, and logs/artifacts/receipts; Docker Manager should be the native surface.
Feature is useful for testing only if it produces ATS capability/harness/strategy/receipt evidence; container startup alone is not completion.
Upstream Coasts architecture and exact token inventory were inspected from `/tmp/pm-upstream-coasts`; no files were edited by the explorer.

recommendation: Good to pursue natively as PM-owned Docker Manager plus Automated Testing capability, using Coasts for source-lineage ideas. Avoid adopting the separate Coasts website/control plane and avoid privileged DinD or remote/secret behavior without explicit PM capability, permission, FileSafe, and receipt design.
